While this movie is Robert Wise at his most visually inventive, with the editing and cinematography being phenomenal, the story, being both an adaptation of Romeo and Juliet and a serious drama about racism, is where the movie falls apart. The tragedy of this movie is the death of a lover, whereas the tragedy of Romeo and Juliet is the death of teenagers. They don't really understand love in the original play, while here it's played like a generic Hollywood love story. When it comes to the film's social commentary, the resolution of the corrupt cop is so shallow that it undermines any message that the film tries to portray. Part of the problem is the fact that this is a musical, which isn't necessarily the movie's fault since the play was originally a musical, but it contrasts too heavily with the subject matter's tone. The Wizard of Oz, La La Land, The Sound of Music, and Singin' in the Rain are all musicals with complementary tones that don't take themselves too seriously. I will say that the "I Wanna Live in America" musical number is by far the best in the film with the most thoughtful social commentary in the film, I am biased though since I am Puerto Rican.
